title: TransferableTypedData for the selectBytes result buffer (rejected)
impact: Exp 234/236 won by wrapping large heap payloads in `TransferableTypedData` to escape the `SendPort` graph copy's GC-heap destination. `selectBytes` returns a large `Uint8List` too, so this tested the same wrap on it. But `selectBytes` bytes are **not** a heap `Uint8List` — they are `result.ptr.asTypedList(length)`, a view over the reader's native `json_buf` (per-reader malloc'd C buffer), snapshotted by the one mandatory `SendPort.send` copy of the `(bytes, rowCount)` record. A/B (prototype behind `RESQLITE_SELECTBYTES_TTD`, reverted) across JSON sizes spanning the 256 KB new-space cap: TTD is **neutral-to-worse at every size** — even at 142/362 KB, ~25% slower at 731 KB (view 1391.7 vs ttd 1742.3 us) — with no GC difference (both lanes the same tiny `Scavenge(external)` stream, sub-0.2 ms pauses). Mechanism: a native-backed view has no GC-heap destination for the wrap to escape; the current path already pays exactly one copy (the snapshot send), and TTD does not remove it — it relocates that copy to a `fromList` memcpy into a fresh external buffer plus malloc/finalizer/ownership-move machinery. Same one copy, extra machinery, so it loses. The mirror image of exp 234/236: the win there came from a heap `Uint8List`'s GC-heap destination, which selectBytes' native view does not have. Rejected; publication-only (prototype reverted). Would reopen only if selectBytes' buffer ever became a heap `Uint8List` instead of a native view.
